headline: Partial refunds were added, but the new code can refund too much and can pay the same refund twice.
what_changed: Support agents can now refund part of a member's order, such as one missed class, by typing an amount.
If the amount is left empty, the refund covers whatever is still unrefunded on the order, as before.
The refund button now says "Refund", and a new field asks for the amount to refund.
The "refund sent" message now promises 5–10 business days instead of 5–10 days.
The "order not found" message now asks the agent to check the order number and try again.
The code no longer blocks a refund on an order that is already fully refunded. Before, it showed an error.
No screen in this copy calls the refund code yet, so agents cannot use it today. The risks below apply once it is connected.

risks.title: Repeated clicks or retries can refund the member twice
risks.explanation: Each refund request now gets a new, unique reference based on the current time. The payment company uses that reference to spot a repeated request, so with a new reference every repeat goes through as a new refund. A double click, a slow connection, or two agents acting at once could each pay out money. The old version used a fixed reference for full refunds, which blocked this.

risks.title: Refund amount is not checked against what was paid
risks.explanation: The typed amount is never compared with the amount paid or the amount already refunded. A typing mistake, such as 200 instead of 20, would refund 200. Removing the old check also means a refund on a fully refunded order now sends a zero or negative amount to the payment company instead of stopping. Those requests may be rejected, or they may be misread by the payment system.

questions_for_developer: Where is the refund button connected to this code, and does that screen check the typed amount before it sends the refund?
Can each refund request carry a stable reference, so that a repeated click or retry cannot pay out the same money twice?
Should the code block any refund larger than the amount still unrefunded, and block refunds on orders that are already fully refunded, as the old version did?
Has the payments team confirmed that "5–10 business days" is the correct timing to show members?
good_news: The change is small and limited to refunds. No stored data is deleted or restructured.
The total already refunded now adds up across several partial refunds, instead of being overwritten by the full amount.
The dollar formatting gives the same output for normal amounts.
